title: Chapter 17. Appendix. Padas signed "Narahari" from the Gaura-pada-tarangini — I: mangalacharana, Gaura's form, abhisheka, kirtana and dance, bhavavesha
html:
Introductory note to the appendix

In the Gaura-pada-tarangini (GPT1 — 1st ed. by Jagadbandhu Bhadra, 1903; GPT2 — 2nd ed., 1934) more than three hundred padas are signed with the name "Narahari" (narahari, "narahari dāsa", "dāsa narahari", "narahari-pahu"). Those also found in the Padakalpataru (PK) were translated in the main part (chapters 1–6): they are padas of Narahari Sarakara, which Majumdar examines as songs of an eyewitness. Here, as a separate appendix, are gathered the padas with the same signature known only from the GPT (and from the Bhakti-ratnakara) — by decision, all are to be translated, with a caveat about attribution.

Narahari is the name of two poets. Narahari Sarakara Thakura of Shrikhanda was an associate of Mahaprabhu, the teacher of Lochana Dasa, a singer of the Lord's bhavas in Navadvipa and Puri; according to the Gaura-ganoddesha-dipika (177), he is Madhumati, an intimate friend of Radha in Vrindavana. Narahari Chakravarti (also called Ghanashyama Dasa), who lived in Vrindavana in the first half of the 18th century, is the author of the Bhakti-ratnakara (BR), Narottama-vilasa, Gita-chandrodaya and other books; in the BR he inserted many of his own songs signed "Narahari" or "Ghanashyama", mostly in Vrajabuli, and often put them in the mouths of the people of Navadvipa while describing the holy places.

The signature alone does not tell whose a pada is. The index of poets in GPT2 divides the "Narahari" padas into three groups: ≈30 of Sarakara (taken from the journal Gauranga-madhuri, published in Shrikhanda), ≈171 of Chakravarti (those found in the BR) and 112 of "Narahari Dasa", undistinguished. Majumdar accepts as Sarakara's only the padas preserved in PK and regards padas known only from the GPT as unreliable; of the "Narahari" padas in the BR, by his analysis, only one belongs to Sarakara (BR p. 924 = PK 2122, chapter 3, no. 1). Sarakara's marks, according to Majumdar, are a simple Bengali without Vrajabuli, without heaped comparisons and alliterations, a correct metre, brevity; ornate Vrajabuli with chains of assonance is Chakravarti's manner. But even the index groups are not beyond doubt: thus pada no. 128 of the section on Gaura's form stands in the index on a page assigned to Sarakara, while in the BR it is put in the mouth of a woman of Nadia (below, no. 8).

Therefore each pada is marked in its heading: "probably Sarakara" — simple Bengali, absent from the BR, assigned by the GPT2 index to Sarakara; "probably Chakravarti" — the pada is in the BR (usually the language too is Vrajabuli with alliterations); "not established" — the arguments conflict or are lacking. In the lila database the padas "probably Chakravarti" have authority B (the author is a recognized acharya, the author of the Bhakti-ratnakara; his authorship is established by his works), the padas "probably Sarakara" and "not established" have authority C; no pada of the appendix has authority D (doubtful authenticity). Chakravarti's padas are a late (18th-century) poetic elaboration of the lilas by a recognized acharya: not the testimony of an eyewitness, but not a forgery either; they often follow the Chaitanya-bhagavata and the Chaitanya-charitamrita. Padas in nagari-bhava (speech of townswomen in love with Gaura) are deferred to the section of nagari padas; padas in which "Narahari" is merely mentioned among the associates while the signature is another's are excluded.

Chapter 17 is the first chapter of the appendix: three padas of mangalacharana (by the GPT2 index — Sarakara's), Gaura's form, the abhisheka in Srivasa's house and arati, kirtana and dance in Navadvipa (a large cycle, almost all of it known also from the BR), bhavavesha — the Lord in the mood of Shiva and in the mood of Krishna. The padas follow the order of the lilas. The base text is GPT1 (tesseract recognition, doubtful places by the IA scan in.ernet.dli.2015.477854) collated with GPT2 and the BR (eds. 1912 and 1960); variants are in the full version of the book. All the padas were also checked against Narahari Chakravarti's Gita-chandrodaya — none of them is there. The notes of the GPT editors are not reproduced.

1. Narahari — "gaura-līlā daraśane icchā baṛa haya mane…" (GPT1 p. 11, no. 27)

Mangalacharana: the poet, seeing Gaura-lila, wishes to write it down in his own tongue but does not know how; the one who will write a book of it is not yet born; the lila of Gaura and Gadadhara, which melts stone, cannot be described even by Sarasvati and Shiva — may at least the poet's few songs help someone to reveal the Lord's lila. Raga pahida. Attribution: probably Sarakara — the GPT2 index assigns the pada to Sarakara; it is not in the BR; simple Bengali tripadi; the poet speaks as an eyewitness, before books on Gaura had appeared.1

গৌরলীলা দরশনে ইচ্ছা বড় হয় মনে ভাষায় লিখিয়া সব রাখি ।
মুঞি ত অতি অধম লিখিতে না জানি ক্রম কেমন করিয়া তাহা লিখি ॥

gauralīlā daraśane icchā baṛa haya mane bhāṣāya likhiyā saba rākhi |
muñi ta ati adhama likhite nā jāni krama kemana kariyā tāhā likhi ||

gaura-līlā daraśane — seeing Gaura's lila; icchā baṛa haya mane — a great wish arises in the heart; bhāṣāya — in the vernacular; likhiyā saba rākhi — to write down and keep it all; muñi ta ati adhama — but I am most lowly; likhite nā jāni krama — I do not know the order of writing; kemana kariyā tāhā likhi — how shall I write it

1.1Seeing Gaura's lila, I greatly long in my heart to write it all down in our own tongue; but I am most lowly, I do not know how to write in due order — how then shall I write it?2

এ গ্রন্থ লিখিবে যে এখনো জন্মে নাই সে জন্মিতে বিলম্ব আছে বহু ।
ভাষায় রচনা হৈলে বুঝিবে লোক সকলে কবে বাঞ্ছা পূরাবেন পহু ॥

e grantha likhibe ye ekhano janme nāi se janmite bilamba āche bahu |
bhāṣāya racanā haile bujhibe loka sakale kabe bāñchā pūrābena pahu ||

e grantha likhibe ye — he who will write this book; ekhano janme nāi se — he is not yet born; janmite bilamba āche bahu — there is long delay before his birth; bhāṣāya racanā haile — when it is composed in the vernacular; bujhibe loka sakale — all people will understand; kabe bāñchā pūrābena pahu — when will the Lord fulfil the wish

1.2He who will write this book is not yet born — long yet is the delay before his birth; when it is composed in our own tongue, all people will understand — when will the Lord fulfil my wish?3

গৌর গদাধর-লীলা আদ্রব করয়ে শিলা কার সাধ্য করিবে বর্ণন ।
সারদা লিখেন যদি নিরন্তর নিরবধি আর সদাশিব পঞ্চানন ॥

gaura gadādhara-līlā ādraba karaye śilā kāra sādhya karibe barṇana |
sāradā likhena yadi nirantara nirabadhi āra sadāśiba pañcānana ||

gaura gadādhara-līlā — the lila of Gaura and Gadadhara; ādraba karaye śilā — softens stone; kāra sādhya — who has the power; karibe barṇana — to describe; sāradā likhena yadi — if Sharada (Sarasvati) wrote; nirantara nirabadhi — ceaselessly, without end; āra sadāśiba pañcānana — and five-faced Sadashiva

1.3The lila of Gaura and Gadadhara softens stone — who has the power to describe it? Even if Sharada were to write ceaselessly, without end, and five-faced Sadashiva with her…4

কিছু কিছু পদ লিখি যদি ইহা কেহ দেখি প্রকাশ করয়ে প্রভুলীলা ।
নরহরি পাবে সুখ ঘুচিবে মনের দুখ গ্রন্থ গানে দরবিবে শিলা ॥

kichu kichu pada likhi yadi ihā keha dekhi prakāśa karaye prabhulīlā |
narahari pābe sukha ghucibe manera dukha grantha gāne darabibe śilā ||

kichu kichu pada likhi — the few songs I write; yadi ihā keha dekhi — if someone, seeing them; prakāśa karaye prabhu-līlā — reveals the Lord's lila; narahari pābe sukha — Narahari will find happiness; ghucibe manera dukha — the grief of the heart will go; grantha gāne — at the singing of the book; darabibe śilā — stones will melt

1.4If, seeing the few songs I write, someone reveals to the world the Lord's lila — Narahari will find happiness, the grief of his heart will go: at the singing of that book stones will melt.

2. Narahari Dasa — "braja-bhūma kari śūnya nadīyāya abatīrṇa…" (GPT1 pp. 11–12, no. 28)

Mangalacharana: an address to Gaura, recognized as the Krishna of Vraja: having emptied Vraja, He has descended in Nadia; there is no peacock feather, no yellow cloth, no flute, no curving pose — yet, since He has let Himself be seen, the mind will not be deceived: this is that very Kanai of Vraja. Raga pahida. Attribution: probably Sarakara — GPT2 index (Sarakara); not in the BR; simple Bengali tripadi.5

ব্রজভূম করি শূন্য নদীয়ায় অবতীর্ণ এতেক তোমার চতুরাল ।
দুঃখ দিয়া নিরন্তর বর্ণ করি ভাবান্তর পুনঃ বাঢ়াও বিরহ-জঞ্জাল ॥

brajabhūma kari śūnya nadīyāya abatīrṇa eteka tomāra caturāla |
duḥkha diyā nirantara barṇa kari bhābāntara punaḥ bāṛhāo biraha-jañjāla ||

braja-bhūma kari śūnya — having emptied the land of Vraja; nadīyāya abatīrṇa — descended in Nadia; eteka tomāra caturāla — such is Your cunning; duḥkha diyā nirantara — giving ceaseless pain; barṇa kari bhābāntara — changing colour and bhava; punaḥ bāṛhāo — again You increase; biraha-jañjāla — the snares of separation

2.1Having emptied the land of Vraja, You descended in Nadia — such is Your cunning! Giving ceaseless pain, having changed colour and bhava, You again multiply the snares of separation.6

নাহি শিখিপুচ্ছ-চূড়া নাই সেই পীতধড়া করে নাই সে মোহন বাঁশরি ।
যে বাঁশরি করি গান বধিলে গোপীর প্রাণ সে বাঁশরি কোথা গৌরহরি ॥

nāhi śikhipuccha-cūṛā nāi sei pītadhaṛā kare nāi se mohana bām̐śari |
ye bām̐śari kari gāna badhile gopīra prāṇa se bām̐śari kothā gaurahari ||

nāhi śikhi-puccha-cūṛā — no crown of peacock feather; nāi sei pīta-dhaṛā — none of that yellow cloth; kare nāi se mohana bām̐śari — in the hand none of that enchanting flute; ye bām̐śari kari gāna — singing with which flute; badhile gopīra prāṇa — You slew the gopis' life; se bām̐śari kothā gaurahari — where is that flute, Gaurahari

2.2There is no crown of peacock feather, none of that yellow cloth, in Your hand none of that enchanting flute — that flute with whose song You stole the very life of the gopis: where is that flute, Gaurahari?

নাহি সে বাঁকা নয়ন এবে হেরি সুলোচন নাই সে ভঙ্গিমা বাঁকা নাই ।
যদি দিলে দরশন এ রূপে ভুলে না মন তুমি সেই ব্রজের কানাই ॥

nāhi se bām̐kā nayana ebe heri sulocana nāi se bhaṅgimā bām̐kā nāi |
yadi dile daraśana e rūpe bhule nā mana tumi sei brajera kānāi ||

nāhi se bām̐kā nayana — none of those slanting eyes; ebe heri sulocana — now I see lovely eyes; nāi se bhaṅgimā — none of that curve (tribhanga); bām̐kā nāi — no bending; yadi dile daraśana — since You gave sight of Yourself; e rūpe bhule nā mana — the mind is not deceived by this form; tumi sei brajera kānāi — You are that Kanai of Vraja

2.3None of those slanting eyes — now I see lovely eyes; none of that curve, none of that bending. But since You have let Yourself be seen, the mind is not deceived by this form: You are that very Kanai of Vraja.7

কহে নরহরি দাস যার নাই বিশ্বাস সে আসিয়া দেখুক নয়নে ।
সে দিনের যেই কথা বলিতে মরমে ব্যথা যে হইল উভয় মিলনে ॥

kahe narahari dāsa yāra nāi biśvāsa se āsiyā dekhuka nayane |
se dinera yei kathā balite marame byathā ye haila ubhaya milane ||

kahe narahari dāsa — says Narahari Dasa; yāra nāi biśvāsa — who has no faith; se āsiyā dekhuka nayane — let him come and see with his eyes; se dinera yei kathā — what happened that day; balite marame byathā — to speak of it is pain in the heart; ye haila ubhaya milane — what took place at the meeting of the two

2.4Says Narahari Dasa: whoever has no faith, let him come and see with his own eyes.
To speak of what happened that day at the meeting of the two is a pain in the heart.8

3. Narahari — "rase tanu ḍharaḍhara gaura-kiśora-bara…" (GPT1 p. 12, no. 29)

Mangalacharana: the Shyama of Dvapara is called Sri Krishna Chaitanya in Kali; within He is Shyama, without golden: to play with Rai in the groves, out of love He became golden; the poet fears to speak of the hidden and cannot keep silent. Raga pahida. Attribution: probably Sarakara — GPT2 index (Sarakara); not in the BR; simple Bengali tripadi.9

রসে তনু ঢরঢর গৌরকিশোরবর এবে নাম শ্রীকৃষ্ণচৈতন্য ।
সে সব নিগূঢ় কথা কহিতে অন্তরে ব্যথা ভক্তি বিনা নাহি জানে অন্য ॥

rase tanu ḍharaḍhara gaurakiśorabara ebe nāma śrīkṛṣṇacaitanya |
se saba nigūṛha kathā kahite antare byathā bhakti binā nāhi jāne anya ||

rase tanu ḍharaḍhara — the body brimming with rasa; gaura-kiśora-bara — the best of youths, Gaura-kishora; ebe nāma śrī-kṛṣṇa-caitanya — now His name is Sri Krishna Chaitanya; se saba nigūṛha kathā — those hidden matters; kahite antare byathā — to tell them is pain in the heart; bhakti binā — without bhakti; nāhi jāne anya — no one else knows

3.1His body brimming with rasa, the best of youths, Gaura-kishora — now His name is Sri Krishna Chaitanya. To speak of these hidden things is a pain in the heart: without bhakti no one else will know them.

দ্বাপর যুগেতে শ্যাম কলিতে চৈতন্য নাম গর্গবাক্য ভাগবতে লিখি ।
চিতে করি অনুমান শ্যাম হৈল গৌরাঙ্গ রাধাকৃষ্ণ-তনু তার সাখী ॥

dvāpara yugete śyāma kalite caitanya nāma gargabākya bhāgabate likhi |
cite kari anumāna śyāma haila gaurāṅga rādhākṛṣṇa-tanu tāra sākhī ||

dvāpara yugete śyāma — in the Dvapara age Shyama; kalite caitanya nāma — in Kali the name Chaitanya; garga-bākya bhāgabate likhi — Garga's words are written in the Bhagavata; cite kari anumāna — I ponder in my heart; śyāma haila gaurāṅga — Shyama became Gauranga; rādhā-kṛṣṇa-tanu — the body of Radha and Krishna; tāra sākhī — is witness to it

3.2In the Dvapara age Shyama, in Kali the name Chaitanya — so are Garga's words written in the Bhagavata. I ponder in my heart: Shyama has become Gauranga — the body of Radha and Krishna is its witness.10

অন্তরেতে শ্যামতনু বাহিরে গৌরাঙ্গ তনু অদ্ভুত গৌরাঙ্গ-লীলা ।
রাই সঙ্গে খেলাইতে কুঞ্জবন বিলাসিতে অনুরাগে গৌরতনু হৈলা ॥

antarete śyāmatanu bāhire gaurāṅga tanu adbhuta gaurāṅga-līlā |
rāi saṅge khelāite kuñjabana bilāsite anurāge gauratanu hailā ||

antarete śyāma-tanu — within the dark body; bāhire gaurāṅga tanu — without the golden body; adbhuta gaurāṅga-līlā — wondrous is Gauranga's lila; rāi saṅge khelāite — to play with Rai; kuñja-bana bilāsite — to enjoy the groves; anurāge — out of love; gaura-tanu hailā — became golden-bodied

3.3Within, the dark body; without, the golden body — wondrous is Gauranga's lila!
To play with Rai, to enjoy the groves, out of love He took the golden body.11

কহিবার কথা নয় কহিলে কি জানি হয় না কহিলে মনে বড় তাপ ।
মনে অনুমান করি গৌরাঙ্গ হৃদয়ে ধরি নরহরি করয়ে বিলাপ ॥

kahibāra kathā naya kahile ki jāni haya nā kahile mane baṛa tāpa |
mane anumāna kari gaurāṅga hṛdaye dhari narahari karaye bilāpa ||

kahibāra kathā naya — it is not a thing to be told; kahile ki jāni haya — if told, who knows what may happen; nā kahile mane baṛa tāpa — if not told, great pain in the heart; mane anumāna kari — pondering in the mind; gaurāṅga hṛdaye dhari — holding Gauranga in the heart; narahari karaye bilāpa — Narahari laments

3.4This is not a thing to be told — who knows what may come of telling it; yet not to tell is great pain in the heart. Pondering in his mind, holding Gauranga in his heart, Narahari laments.

(catalogue: NG-001). Not in PK, the BR, the Kshanada-gita-chintamani (KGC) or the Padamrita-samudra (PS). The index of poets of GPT2 assigns p. 8 (padas nos. 27–29) to Narahari Sarakara (from the journal Gauranga-madhuri); the language is simple Bengali tripadi without Vrajabuli, which fits Majumdar's marks of Sarakara. But the pada is known only from the GPT; C. written in Sanskrit. Gaura. Whom the poet awaits he does not say; Bengali poems on the Lord were written by Vrindavana Dasa (Chaitanya-bhagavata) and by Lochana Dasa, a disciple of Narahari Sarakara, who calls him his Thakura (Chaitanya-mangala, Sutra-khanda, ch. 1, vv. 9, 61). inseparable associate of the Lord (in Krishna-lila — Radha): "the lila of Gaura and Gadadhara" is a favourite theme of Narahari Sarakara (cf. chapter 3, no. 1). catalogue (new row NG-236): the stage-1 catalogue missed it. Not in PK, BR, KGC, PS. GPT2 index — Sarakara (p. 8). C. (CC Adi 1.5; ch. 4). The speaker is a resident of Vraja who has recognized Krishna in Gaura: "the snares of separation" are his separation from Krishna, who has left Vraja for Nadia. an endearing name of Krishna in Vraja. Cf. CC Madhya 8 (Ramananda Raya sees Krishna in the Lord). Krishna to an associate who recognized Him. (new row NG-237). Not in PK, BR, KGC, PS. GPT2 index — Sarakara (p. 8). C. Kali the name Chaitanya" are not in Garga: this is the poet's interpretation; CC Adi 3.36–40 sees in the "yellow" (pīta) colour an indication of the golden avatara of the Kali age. "The body of Radha and Krishna" — Gaura, Radha and Krishna united in one form (CC Adi 1.5; 4.55–56). wishing to taste Radha's love, took Her bhava and golden lustre (CC Adi 1.6; ch. 4); the golden colour is Her colour, not a worldly passion.

4. Narahari — "nācata bhubana-mano-mohana…" (GPT1 p. 135, no. 70; BR)

Gaura's form in the dance: His colour brighter than champaka, gold and lotus, His body in sandal paste and Chinese silk, His face gentler than moons, His brows a row of bees, necklace and earrings swaying, curls scattering, His tendril-like hands playing, His feet keeping the rhythm. Raga karnata. Attribution: probably Chakravarti — the pada is in the BR (12th wave); Vrajabuli with chains of comparisons.12

নাচত ভুবনমনোমোহন চম্পক কনক কঞ্জ জিনি বরণা ।
সুবলিত তনু মৃদু মলয়জ-রঞ্জিত পহিরণ চীন বসন ঘন কিরণা ॥

nācata bhubanamanomohana campaka kanaka kañja jini baraṇā |
subalita tanu mṛdu malayaja-rañjita pahiraṇa cīna basana ghana kiraṇā ||

nācata — dances; bhubana-mano-mohana — the Enchanter of the minds of the world; campaka kanaka kañja jini baraṇā — whose colour surpasses champaka, gold and lotus; subalita tanu mṛdu — shapely tender body; malayaja-rañjita — anointed with sandal; pahiraṇa cīna basana — wearing Chinese silk; ghana kiraṇā — densely shining

4.1He dances, the Enchanter of the minds of all the worlds — His colour surpassing champaka, gold and lotus; His shapely, tender body anointed with sandal, He wears garments of Chinese silk, densely shining.

হিমকর-নিকর-নিন্দি মধুরানন হাসত মধুর সুধা যনু ঝরঈ ।
ভুরুযুগ ভৃঙ্গ-পাঁতি লস লোচন ডগমগ অরুণ-কিরণ-ভর হরঈ ॥

himakara-nikara-nindi madhurānana hāsata madhura sudhā yanu jharaī |
bhuruyuga bhṛṅga-pām̐ti lasa locana ḍagamaga aruṇa-kiraṇa-bhara haraī ||

himakara-nikara-nindi — putting to shame hosts of moons; madhurānana — sweet face; hāsata madhura — smiles sweetly; sudhā yanu jharaī — as if nectar flows; bhuru-yuga bhṛṅga-pām̐ti — the brows a row of bees; lasa locana — the eyes shine; ḍagamaga — swaying; aruṇa-kiraṇa-bhara haraī — rob the dawn's rays of their weight

4.2His sweet face puts to shame hosts of moons; sweetly He smiles — as if nectar were flowing; His brows a row of bees; His eyes gleam and sway, robbing the dawn's rays of their power.13

দোলত মণিময় হার হরত ধৃতি টলমল কুণ্ডল ঝলকত শ্রবণে ।
চাঁচর চিকুর-ভঙ্গি-ভার-ভরে বিলুলিত হালত তিমির-তার যনু পবনে ॥

dolata maṇimaya hāra harata dhṛti ṭalamala kuṇḍala jhalakata śrabaṇe |
cām̐cara cikura-bhaṅgi-bhāra-bhare bilulita hālata timira-tāra yanu pabane ||

dolata maṇimaya hāra — the jewelled necklace sways; harata dhṛti — stealing composure; ṭalamala kuṇḍala — earrings tremble; jhalakata śrabaṇe — flashing at the ears; cām̐cara cikura-bhaṅgi-bhāra-bhare — under the weight of the curling locks; bilulita hālata — scattered, they sway; timira-tāra yanu pabane — like strands of darkness in the wind

4.3The jewelled necklace sways, stealing all composure; the earrings tremble, flashing at His ears; His curling locks, under their own weight, scatter and sway like strands of darkness in the wind.

অভিনয় ললিত কলিত কর-কিশলয়ে কত শত তাল ধরত পগ ধরণে ।
নরহরি পরম উলস যশ গায়ত শোভা বিপুল কৌনক বিবরণে ॥

abhinaya lalita kalita kara-kiśalaye kata śata tāla dharata paga dharaṇe |
narahari parama ulasa yaśa gāyata śobhā bipula kaunaka bibaraṇe ||

abhinaya lalita — graceful play; kalita kara-kiśalaye — performed with tendril-like hands; kata śata tāla dharata — keeps hundreds of rhythms; paga dharaṇe — in placing His feet; narahari parama ulasa — Narahari in great delight; yaśa gāyata — sings the glory; śobhā bipula — the boundless beauty; kaunaka bibaraṇe — who can describe

4.4In graceful play of His tendril-like hands, stepping on the earth, He keeps hundreds of rhythms; Narahari, in great delight, sings His glory: who can describe this boundless beauty?

5. Narahari — "nadīyāra mājhāre nācaye gorācām̐da…" (GPT1 p. 135, no. 72; BR)

Gaura's form, from face to feet: Gorachand dancing in the midst of Nadia is a snare for every heart; seeing Him, the young wives lose their senses; His face is the autumn moon, His speech nectar, His eyes the abode of love, His brows shame Kama's bow, His curls are twined with malati, on His brow a drop of sandal; garland, long arms, slender waist, feet before whose nails Kama swoons — this is the Nagara of Gokula, the ocean of rasa. Raga kamoda. Attribution: probably Chakravarti — the pada is in the BR (12th wave, among the songs of the people of Nadia).14

নদীয়ার মাঝারে নাচয়ে গোরাচাঁদ ।
অখিল জনার মন বান্ধিবার ফাঁদ ॥

nadīyāra mājhāre nācaye gorācām̐da |
akhila janāra mana bāndhibāra phām̐da ||

nadīyāra mājhāre — in the midst of Nadia; nācaye gorācām̐da — Gorachand dances; akhila janāra mana — the hearts of all people; bāndhibāra phām̐da — a snare to bind

5.1In the midst of Nadia dances Gorachand —
a snare to capture the hearts of all people.

কনক কেশর তনু অনুপম ছটা ।
দেখিতে মোহিত নব যুবতীর ঘটা ॥

kanaka keśara tanu anupama chaṭā |
dekhite mohita naba yubatīra ghaṭā ||

kanaka keśara tanu — body like golden filaments; anupama chaṭā — peerless radiance; dekhite mohita — seeing Him are bewitched; naba yubatīra ghaṭā — crowds of young wives

5.2His body like golden filaments, His radiance beyond compare;
seeing Him, crowds of young wives lose their senses.15

শরদের চাঁদ কি মধুর মুখখানি ।
অমিয়ার ধারা বাণী তাপিয়া জুড়ানি ॥

śaradera cām̐da ki madhura mukhakhāni |
amiyāra dhārā bāṇī tāpiyā juṛāni ||

śaradera cām̐da — the autumn moon; ki madhura mukha-khāni — how sweet the face; amiyāra dhārā bāṇī — speech a stream of nectar; tāpiyā juṛāni — cooling the afflicted

5.3How sweet His face — the autumn moon!
His speech a stream of nectar, cooling the afflicted.

ঈষৎ মিশাল হাসি অধর উজ্জ্বল ।
দশন মুকুতাপাঁতি করে ঝলমল ॥

īṣat miśāla hāsi adhara ujjvala |
daśana mukutāpām̐ti kare jhalamala ||

īṣat miśāla hāsi — mingled slightly with a smile; adhara ujjvala — the lips shine; daśana mukutā-pām̐ti — the teeth a row of pearls; kare jhalamala — flash

5.4Slightly mingled with a smile, His lips shine;
the pearl-row of His teeth flashes.

নয়নযুগল অনুরাগের আলয় ।
চাহনিতে ভুবন-পরাণ হরি লয় ॥

nayanayugala anurāgera ālaya |
cāhanite bhubana-parāṇa hari laya ||

nayana-yugala — the pair of eyes; anurāgera ālaya — abode of love; cāhanite — with a glance; bhubana-parāṇa — the life of the world; hari laya — steals away

5.5His eyes are the abode of love;
with a glance He steals the life of the whole world.

কামের ধনুক-মদ ভাঙ্গিবার তরে ।
কেবা গঢ়াইল ভুরু কত রঙ্গ ধরে ॥

kāmera dhanuka-mada bhāṅgibāra tare |
kebā gaṛhāila bhuru kata raṅga dhare ||

kāmera dhanuka-mada — the pride of Kama's bow; bhāṅgibāra tare — in order to break; kebā gaṛhāila bhuru — who fashioned the brows; kata raṅga dhare — so full of play

5.6Who carved these brows — so full of play —
to break the pride of Kama's bow?

চাঁচর কেশের ঝুঁটা চমকিয়া বাঁকে ।
মালতী-বলিত অলি ফিরে ঝাঁকে ঝাঁকে ॥

cām̐cara keśera jhum̐ṭā camakiyā bām̐ke |
mālatī-balita ali phire jhām̐ke jhām̐ke ||

cām̐cara keśera jhum̐ṭā — the knot of curling hair; camakiyā bām̐ke — flashing, bends aside; mālatī-balita — twined with malati; ali phire jhām̐ke jhām̐ke — bees circle in swarms

5.7The knot of His curling hair, flashing, is bent aside;
around the malati twined in it, swarms of bees are circling.

কে ধরে ধৈরজ হেরি সুচারু কপাল ।
চন্দনের বিন্দু ইন্দু-গরবের কাল ॥

ke dhare dhairaja heri sucāru kapāla |
candanera bindu indu-garabera kāla ||

ke dhare dhairaja — who keeps composure; heri sucāru kapāla — seeing the lovely brow; candanera bindu — the drop of sandal; indu-garabera kāla — death to the moon's pride

5.8Who can keep composure, seeing that lovely brow?
The drop of sandal on it is death to the moon's pride.

ভুবনবিজয়ী মালা দোলয়ে হিয়ায় ।
বারেক নিরখি আঁখি সদাই ধিয়ায় ॥

bhubanabijayī mālā dolaye hiyāya |
bāreka nirakhi ām̐khi sadāi dhiyāya ||

bhubana-bijayī mālā — the world-conquering garland; dolaye hiyāya — sways on the breast; bāreka nirakhi ām̐khi — the eye that has seen it once; sadāi dhiyāya — ever meditates on it

5.9On His breast sways the garland that has conquered the world;
whoever has seen it once keeps his eyes on it and remembers it ever.

কিবা সে দীঘল ভুজযুগের বলনী ।
কত ভাতি ভঙ্গী সতীকুলের দলনী ॥

kibā se dīghala bhujayugera balanī |
kata bhāti bhaṅgī satīkulera dalanī ||

kibā se dīghala bhuja-yugera balanī — how graceful the curve of the long arms; kata bhāti bhaṅgī — how many movements; satī-kulera dalanī — crushing (the steadfastness of) the chaste

5.10How graceful the curve of His long arms!
How many movements in them — crushing the steadfastness of the chaste.

সরুয়া কাঁকালি কিবা মুঠেতে লুকায় ।
বিনি মূলে কিনে মন নয়ন জুড়ায় ॥

saruyā kām̐kāli kibā muṭhete lukāya |
bini mūle kine mana nayana juṛāya ||

saruyā kām̐kāli — slender waist; kibā muṭhete lukāya — would hide in a fist; bini mūle kine mana — buys hearts without price; nayana juṛāya — refreshes the eyes

5.11His slender waist — it would hide within a fist;
without price He buys hearts and refreshes the eyes.

চরণ-কমলতল অতি অনুপাম ।
নখর-নিকরে কত মূরছয়ে কাম ॥

caraṇa-kamalatala ati anupāma |
nakhara-nikare kata mūrachaye kāma ||

caraṇa-kamala-tala — the soles of the lotus feet; ati anupāma — beyond compare; nakhara-nikare — before the host of nails; kata mūrachaye kāma — many a Kama swoons

5.12The soles of His lotus feet are beyond compare;
before the radiance of His nails many a Kama swoons.16

কহে নরহরি কি না জানে রঙ্গ তার ।
গোকুলনাগর ও রসের পাথার ॥

kahe narahari ki nā jāne raṅga tāra |
gokulanāgara o rasera pāthāra ||

kahe narahari — says Narahari; ki nā jāne raṅga tāra — what play of His does He not know; gokula-nāgara — the Nagara of Gokula; o rasera pāthāra — that ocean of rasa

5.13Says Narahari: what play does He not know! —
the Nagara of Gokula, that ocean of rasa.17

6. Narahari — "suradhunī-tīre gaura naṭa-nāgara…" (GPT1 p. 136, no. 73; BR)

Gaura's dance on the bank of the Suradhuni: Gaura, the graceful dancer, sports with His associates, captivating the eyes of the world; His body outshines a golden mountain, His arms put to shame an elephant's trunk, again and again He cries "Hari, Hari!"; seeing Gadadhara, He sheds tears like a cloud of the month of Shravana, and the earth trembles beneath His feet. Raga somaraga. Attribution: probably Chakravarti — the pada is in the BR (12th wave); Vrajabuli.18

সুরধুনীতীরে গৌর নটনাগর পরিকর সঙ্গে রঙ্গে বিহরে ।
নিরুপম বিবিধ নৃত্য নব মাধুরী নিখিল ভুবনজন-নয়ন হরে ॥

suradhunītīre gaura naṭanāgara parikara saṅge raṅge bihare |
nirupama bibidha nṛtya naba mādhurī nikhila bhubanajana-nayana hare ||

suradhunī-tīre — on the bank of the Suradhuni (Ganga); gaura naṭa-nāgara — Gaura the graceful dancer; parikara saṅge raṅge bihare — sports with the associates; nirupama bibidha nṛtya — peerless varied dance; naba mādhurī — ever-new sweetness; nikhila bhubana-jana-nayana hare — steals the eyes of all the people of the world

6.1On the bank of the Suradhuni, Gaura, the graceful dancer, sports together with His associates; the peerless, many-sided dance, ever-new sweetness — steals the eyes of all the people of the world.

কনক-ধরাধর-গরবহারী তনু ঝলমল বিপুল পুলকনিকরে ।
কুঞ্জর-কর-মদ-হর ভুজ-ভঙ্গিম নিন্দই কত শত কুসুমশরে ॥

kanaka-dharādhara-garabahārī tanu jhalamala bipula pulakanikare |
kuñjara-kara-mada-hara bhuja-bhaṅgima nindai kata śata kusumaśare ||

kanaka-dharādhara-garaba-hārī tanu — the body robbing a golden mountain of its pride; jhalamala — shines; bipula pulaka-nikare — with abundant thrills; kuñjara-kara-mada-hara — humbling an elephant's trunk; bhuja-bhaṅgima — the curve of the arms; nindaī kata śata kusumaśare — puts to shame hundreds of Kamas

6.2His body, robbing a golden mountain of its pride, shines with abundant thrills; the curve of His arms, which surpass an elephant's trunk, puts to shame hundreds of Kamas.19

কুন্দ-দশন-দ্যুতি দমকত মঞ্জুল মিলিত সুহাস মধুর অধরে ।
ডগমগ বদন বদত ঘন হরি হরি শুনইতে কো আছু ধৈরজ ধরে ॥

kunda-daśana-dyuti damakata mañjula milita suhāsa madhura adhare |
ḍagamaga badana badata ghana hari hari śunaite ko āchu dhairaja dhare ||

kunda-daśana-dyuti — the lustre of the kunda-like teeth; damakata mañjula — flashes lovely; milita suhāsa madhura adhare — in a soft smile on the sweet lips; ḍagamaga badana — the face sways; badata ghana hari hari — says ceaselessly "Hari, Hari"; śunaite ko āchu dhairaja dhare — who, hearing it, keeps composure

6.3His teeth flash, lovely — the lustre of kunda flowers — in a soft smile on His sweet lips; His face sways, His lips cry ceaselessly "Hari, Hari!" — who, hearing it, can keep composure?

উমড়ই হৃদয় গদাধরে হেরইতে শাঙন-ঘন সম নয়ন ঝরে ।
নরহরি ভণত ধরণী করু টলমল সুললিত চঞ্চল চরণ-ভরে ॥

umaṛai hṛdaya gadādhare heraite śāṅana-ghana sama nayana jhare |
narahari bhaṇata dharaṇī karu ṭalamala sulalita cañcala caraṇa-bhare ||

umaḍaī hṛdaya — the heart overflows; gadādhare heraite — on seeing Gadadhara; śām̐ṅana-ghana sama — like a cloud of Shravana; nayana jhare — the eyes pour; narahari bhaṇata — says Narahari; dharaṇī karu ṭalamala — the earth trembles; sulalita cañcala caraṇa-bhare — under the weight of the lovely restless feet

6.4His heart overflows when He sees Gadadhara: His eyes pour tears like a cloud in the month of Shravana; says Narahari: the earth trembles under the weight of His lovely, light feet.20

7. Narahari — "biharata surasarita-tīra…" (GPT1 pp. 151–152, no. 119; BR)

Gaura's form on the bank of the Ganga, from face to feet: youthful, He sports by the river; His colour outshines lightning, gold and kunkuma, His face is a snare for the eyes of young wives, His curls dark clouds, His brows serpents; broad chest, slender waist, lotus feet about which bee-devotees hover; a cloud of mercy, He ever showers the nectar of prema — only foolish Narahari it does not touch. Raga nataraga. Attribution: probably Chakravarti — the pada is in the BR (12th wave); Vrajabuli with strings of comparisons.21

বিহরত সুরসরিত-তীর গৌর তরুণ বয়স থির তড়িত-কনক-কুঙ্কুম-মদ-মর্দন তনুকাঁতি ।
মদন-কদন বদনচন্দ্র নিখিল-তরুণী-নয়ান-ফন্দ হসত লসত দশনবৃন্দ কুন্দকুসুমপাঁতি ॥

biharata surasarita-tīra gaura taruṇa bayasa thira taṛita-kanaka-kuṅkuma-mada-mardana tanukām̐ti | madana-kadana badanacandra nikhila-taruṇī-nayāna-phanda hasata lasata daśanabṛnda kundakusumapām̐ti ||

biharata surasarita-tīra — strolls by the bank of the heavenly river; gaura taruṇa bayasa thira — Gaura, young, of unchanging youth; taṛita-kanaka-kuṅkuma-mada-mardana — crushing the pride of lightning, gold and kunkuma; tanu-kām̐ti — the lustre of the body; madana-kadana badana-candra — the moon-face tormenting Madana; nikhila-taruṇī-nayāna-phanda — a snare for the eyes of all young wives; hasata lasata daśana-bṛnda — smiling, the teeth gleam; kunda-kusuma-pām̐ti — a row of kunda flowers

7.1By the bank of the heavenly river strolls Gaura — young, in unchanging youth: the lustre of His body crushes the pride of lightning, gold and kunkuma; His moon-face torments Madana, a snare for the eyes of all young wives; in His smile His teeth gleam — a row of kunda flowers.

অঞ্জন-ঘন-পুঞ্জ-বরণ কুঞ্চিত কচ ধৈরজ-হরণ বেশ বিমল অলকাকুল রাজত অনুপাম ।
ভাল-তিলক ঝলকত অতি ভাঙ-ভুজগ মঞ্জুল গতি চঞ্চল দিঠে অঞ্চল রসরঞ্জিত ছবিধাম ॥

añjana-ghana-puñja-baraṇa kuñcita kaca dhairaja-haraṇa beśa bimala alakākula rājata anupāma | bhāla-tilaka jhalakata ati bhāṅa-bhujaga mañjula gati cañcala diṭhe añcala rasarañjita chabidhāma ||

añjana-ghana-puñja-baraṇa — the colour of dense collyrium; kuñcita kaca — curling locks; dhairaja-haraṇa — stealing composure; beśa bimala — pure attire; alakākula rājata anupāma — the scattered tresses shine peerless; bhāla-tilaka jhalakata ati — the tilaka on the brow flashes brightly; bhām̐ṅa-bhujaga mañjula gati — the brows, serpents of graceful motion; cañcala diṭhe añcala — the corners of the restless eyes; rasa-rañjita chabidhāma — tinged with rasa, an abode of beauty

7.2The colour of dense collyrium, His curling locks steal composure; peerless shine His pure attire and scattered tresses; the tilaka on His brow flashes brightly, His brows are gracefully gliding serpents; the corners of His restless eyes, tinged with rasa, are an abode of beauty.22

কুণ্ডল শ্রুতি গণ্ড কলিত কণ্ঠহি বনমাল বলিত বাহু বিপুল বলয়া কর কোমল বলিহারি ।
পরিসর বর বক্ষ অতুল নাশত কত কুলবধূকুল ললিত কটি সুকৃশ কেশরী-গরব-খরবকারী ॥

kuṇḍala śruti gaṇḍa kalita kaṇṭhahi banamāla balita bāhu bipula balayā kara komala balihāri | parisara bara bakṣa atula nāśata kata kulabadhūkula lalita kaṭi sukṛśa keśarī-garaba-kharabakārī ||

kuṇḍala śruti gaṇḍa kalita — the earrings at the ears touch the cheeks; kaṇṭhahi banamāla balita — on the neck the forest garland; bāhu bipula — long arms; balayā kara komala — bracelets, tender palms; balihāri — I give my life for them; parisara bara bakṣa atula — broad, peerless chest; nāśata kata kulabadhū-kula — destroys (the steadfastness of) many noble wives; lalita kaṭi sukṛśa — graceful slender waist; keśarī-garaba-kharabakārī — humbling the pride of the lion

7.3Earrings touch His cheeks, on His neck the forest garland; long arms, bracelets, tender palms — I give my life for them! His broad, peerless chest destroys the steadfastness of many a noble wife; His graceful, slender waist humbles the pride of the lion.

ডগমগ ভুজ জানু তরুণ অরুণাবলী কিরণ চরণ কমল মধুর সৌরভভরে ভকত-ভ্রমর ভোর ।

nṛtyata gauracandra jana-rañjana — dances Gaurachandra, delight of the people; nityānanda bipada-bhaya-bhañjana — Nityananda, destroyer of the fear of calamity; kañja-nayana jiti naba naba khañjana — lotus eyes surpassing ever-new khanjanas; cāhani manamatha-garaba hare — the glance steals Kama's pride; jhalakata duhum̐ tanu kanaka-dharādhara — both bodies flash, golden mountains; naṭana ghaṭana paga dharata dharaṇī para — in the dance the feet strike the earth; hāsa milita mukha lasata sudhākara — faces mingled with smiles shine like moons; ucari bacana janu amiya jhare — when they speak, it is as if nectar flowed

14.1Gaurachandra, the delight of the people, and Nityananda, the destroyer of the fear of calamity, dance: Their lotus eyes surpass ever-new khanjana birds, Their glance steals Kama's pride; both bodies flash — golden mountains; in the dance Their feet strike the earth; Their faces, mingled with smiles, shine like moons; when They speak, it is as if nectar were flowing.49

শোভা নিরুপম ভণত না আয়ত বেষ্টিত পরিকর গুণগণ গায়ত মধুর মধুর মৃদু মর্দল বায়ত ধাধা ধিগি ধিগি ধিকট ধিলঙ্গ । গণ সহ সুরগণ গগন-পন্থ-গত ঘন ঘন সরস কুসুমবর বরষত জয় জয় জয় ধ্বনি ভুবন বিয়াপত নরহরি কহব কি প্রেম-তরঙ্গ ॥

śobhā nirupama bhaṇata nā āyata beṣṭita parikara guṇagaṇa gāyata madhura madhura mṛdu mardala bāyata dhādhā dhigi dhigi dhikaṭa dhilaṅga | gaṇa saha suragaṇa gagana-pantha-gata ghana ghana sarasa kusumabara baraṣata jaya jaya jaya dhvani bhubana biyāpata narahari kahaba ki prema-taraṅga ||

śobhā nirupama — peerless beauty; bhaṇata nā āyata — cannot be told; beṣṭita parikara — surrounding, the associates; guṇa-gaṇa gāyata — sing the virtues; madhura madhura mṛdu mardala bāyata — sweetly, softly the mardala plays; dhādhā dhigi dhigi dhikaṭa dhilaṅga — rhythm syllables; gaṇa saha sura-gaṇa — the gods with their retinues; gagana-pantha-gata — on the paths of the sky; ghana ghana sarasa kusuma-bara baraṣata — again and again shower choice flowers; jaya jaya jaya dhvani bhubana biyāpata — the cry "jaya" fills the world; narahari kahaba ki prema-taraṅga — what can Narahari say of the waves of prema

14.2Peerless is this beauty — it cannot be told; surrounding Them, the associates sing Their virtues; sweetly, sweetly, softly the mardala plays: "dha-dha, dhigi-dhigi, dhikat, dhilanga"; the gods with their retinues on the paths of the sky again and again shower choice flowers; the cry "Jaya, jaya, jaya" fills the world — what can Narahari say of the waves of prema?

15. Narahari — "āju ki ānanda saṅkīrtane…" (GPT1 p. 262, no. 46; BR)

The sankirtana of Gaura and Nityananda: all are beside themselves with prema, from everyone's eyes rivers of tears flow, some fall on one another, others roar, tremble, embrace one another and cannot let go, take the dust of one another's feet and roll on the ground; Lord and servants are all alike in this. Raga kamoda. Attribution: probably Chakravarti — the pada is in the BR (12th wave); simple Bengali tripadi.50

আজু কি আনন্দ সংকীর্তনে ।
নাচে গৌর নিত্যানন্দ পরম আনন্দকন্দ প্রিয় পারিষদবৃন্দ সনে ॥ ধ্রু ॥

āju ki ānanda saṃkīrtane |
nāce gaura nityānanda parama ānandakanda priya pāriṣadabṛnda sane || dhru ||

āju ki ānanda saṅkīrtane — what bliss today in the sankirtana; nāce gaura nityānanda — Gaura and Nityananda dance; parama ānanda-kanda — the root of supreme bliss; priya pāriṣada-bṛnda sane — with the dear associates

15.1(Refrain) What bliss today in the sankirtana!
Gaura and Nityananda dance — the root of supreme bliss — together with Their dear associates.

নাচে বোলে ভাল ভাল বাজে খোল করতাল সবে মহা বিহ্বল প্রেমায় ।
নদীর প্রবাহ-পারা সবার নয়নে ধারা কেহ কেহ পড়ে কারু গায় ॥

nāce bole bhāla bhāla bāje khola karatāla sabe mahā bihvala premāya |
nadīra prabāha-pārā sabāra nayane dhārā keha keha paṛe kāru gāya ||

nāce bole bhāla bhāla — dancing, they cry "well done, well done"; bāje khola karatāla — khol and kartals resound; sabe mahā bihvala premāya — all are beside themselves with prema; nadīra prabāha-pārā — like the current of a river; sabāra nayane dhārā — streams from everyone's eyes; keha keha paṛe kāru gāya — some fall on one another

15.2Dancing, they cry: "Well done, well done!"; khol and kartals resound — all are beside themselves with prema; from everyone's eyes pour streams like the current of a river; some fall upon one another.

কেহ বা পুলকভরে হুঙ্কার গর্জন করে কাঁপে কেহ থির হৈতে নারে ।
কেহ কারু পানে চাঞা দুই বাহু পসারিয়া কোলে করি ছাড়িতে না পারে ॥

keha bā pulakabhare huṅkāra garjana kare kām̐pe keha thira haite nāre |
keha kāru pāne cāñā dui bāhu pasāriyā kole kari chāṛite nā pāre ||

keha vā pulaka-bhare — someone, thrilling; huṅkāra garjana kare — roars and shouts; kām̐pe keha — someone trembles; thira haite nāre — cannot stand steady; keha kāru pāne cāñā — someone, looking at another; dui bāhu pasāriyā — spreading both arms; kole kari chāṛite nā pāre — embraces and cannot let go

15.3Someone, thrilling, roars and shouts aloud; someone trembles, unable to stand steady; someone, looking at another, opens his arms, embraces him — and cannot let him go.

কেহ কারু পায় ধরে পদধূলি লয় শিরে কেহ ভূমে পড়ি গড়ি যায় ।
প্রভু ভৃত্য এক রীতি দেখি নরহরি অতি আনন্দে প্রভুর গুণ গায় ॥

keha kāru pāya dhare padadhūli laya śire keha bhūme paṛi gaṛi yāya |
prabhu bhṛtya eka rīti dekhi narahari ati ānande prabhura guṇa gāya ||

keha kāru pāya dhare — someone seizes another's feet; pada-dhūli laya śire — puts the dust of the feet on his head; keha bhūme paṛi gaṛi yāya — someone falls to the ground and rolls; prabhu bhṛtya eka rīti — Lord and servants in one state; dekhi narahari ati ānande — seeing this, Narahari in great bliss; prabhura guṇa gāya — sings the Lord's virtues

15.4Someone seizes another's feet and puts the dust of his feet on his head; someone, falling to the ground, rolls in the dust; Lord and servants are in one state: seeing this, Narahari in great bliss sings the virtues of the Lord.51

16. Narahari — "nācata gaurāṅga-cām̐da bibhora bhābete…" (GPT1 p. 262, no. 47)

Gauranga dances, seized by bhava; in the same bhava, on His left, Gadadhara dances; Nitai follows behind so that His golden body may not fall to the ground; the Lord embraces the fallen. Raga pathamanjari. Attribution: not established — the pada is not in the BR (the GPT2 index, however, assigns its page to Chakravarti); simple Bengali payar.52

নাচত গৌরাঙ্গচাঁদ বিভোর ভাবেতে ।
সেই ভাবে গদাধর নাচয়ে বামেতে ॥

nācata gaurāṅgacām̐da bibhora bhābete |
sei bhābe gadādhara nācaye bāmete ||

nācata gaurāṅga-cām̐da — Gaurangachand dances; bibhora bhābete — seized by bhava; sei bhābe gadādhara — in the same bhava Gadadhara; nācaye bāmete — dances on the left

16.1Gaurangachand dances, seized by bhava;
in the same bhava on His left dances Gadadhara.

ভাদর-সোণার অঙ্গ ভূমে পড়ে পাছে ।
তাই সে নিতাইচাঁদ ফিরে পাছে পাছে ॥

bhādara-soṇāra aṅga bhūme paṛe pāche |
tāi se nitāicām̐da phire pāche pāche ||

bhādara-soṇāra aṅga — the body of pure gold; bhūme paṛe pāche — lest it fall to the ground; tāi se nitāicām̐da — that is why Nitaichand; phire pāche pāche — keeps close behind

16.2Lest His body of pure gold should fall to the ground,
Nitaichand keeps following close behind Him.53

নাচে রে গৌরাঙ্গ আমার হেলিয়া দুলিয়া ।
বাজে খোল করতাল তাধিয়া তাধিয়া ॥

nāce re gaurāṅga āmāra heliyā duliyā |
bāje khola karatāla tādhiyā tādhiyā ||

nāce re gaurāṅga āmāra — my Gauranga dances; heliyā duliyā — swaying, rocking; bāje khola karatāla — khol and kartals sound; tādhiyā tādhiyā — "ta-dhiya, ta-dhiya"

16.3My Gauranga dances, swaying, rocking;
khol and kartals sound: "ta-dhiya, ta-dhiya".

দুরগত পতিত ধরিয়া করু কোর ।
পামর এ নরহরি ও না রসে ভোর ॥

duragata patita dhariyā karu kora |
pāmara e narahari o nā rase bhora ||

duragata patita — the fallen who have gone astray; dhariyā karu kora — He seizes and embraces; pāmara e narahari — only sinful Narahari; o nā rase bhora — is not immersed in that rasa

16.4He seizes and embraces the fallen who have gone astray —
only sinful Narahari is not immersed in this rasa.

17. Narahari — "nācata gauracandra guṇadhāma…" (GPT1 p. 263, no. 49; BR)

Gaura's dance: the radiance of His body outshines a golden mountain and lightning; His smile steals composure, earrings tremble, curls are decked with flowers, a garland on His chest, His arms in new play, His feet keeping the rhythm; the associates sing, khol and khamak resound. Raga bangala. Attribution: probably Chakravarti — the pada is in the BR (12th wave); Vrajabuli.54

নাচত গৌরচন্দ্র গুণধাম ।
ঝলকত অঙ্গ-কিরণ মনরঞ্জন কনক-মেরু দূরে দামিনী-দাম ॥ ধ্রু ॥

nācata gauracandra guṇadhāma |
jhalakata aṅga-kiraṇa manarañjana kanaka-meru dūre dāminī-dāma || dhru ||

nācata gauracandra guṇadhāma — Gaurachandra dances, abode of virtues; jhalakata aṅga-kiraṇa — the radiance of the body flashes; mana-rañjana — charming the heart; kanaka-meru dūre — (casting) far away golden Meru; dāminī-dāma — and garlands of lightning

17.1(Refrain) Gaurachandra dances, the abode of virtues; the radiance of His body flashes, charming the heart — it casts far away both golden Meru and garlands of lightning.

বন্ধুর বদন মদন-মদ-মরদন মধুরিম হাস যুবতী-ধৃতি-হারী ।
শ্রুতি জিতি তরুণ-অরুণ মণিকুণ্ডল টলমল নয়নযুগল ছবি ভারি ॥

bandhura badana madana-mada-maradana madhurima hāsa yubatī-dhṛti-hārī |
śruti jiti taruṇa-aruṇa maṇikuṇḍala ṭalamala nayanayugala chabi bhāri ||

bandhura badana — the lovely face; madana-mada-maradana — crushing Madana's pride; madhurima hāsa — the sweet smile; yubatī-dhṛti-hārī — stealing the composure of young wives; śruti jiti taruṇa-aruṇa maṇi-kuṇḍala — at the ears jewelled earrings surpassing the young dawn; ṭalamala nayana-yugala — both eyes sway; chabi bhāri — great is their beauty

17.2His lovely face crushes Madana's pride; His sweet smile steals the composure of young wives; at His ears tremble jewelled earrings surpassing the young dawn; both His eyes sway — how beautiful they are!55

চাঁচর চিকণ কেশ কুসুমাঞ্চিত চপল চারু উরে মণ্ডিত মাল ।
অভিনব বাহুভঙ্গী ভর নিরুপম ধরত চরণতলে সুললিত তাল ॥

cām̐cara cikaṇa keśa kusumāñcita capala cāru ure maṇḍita māla |
abhinaba bāhubhaṅgī bhara nirupama dharata caraṇatale sulalita tāla ||

cām̐cara cikaṇa keśa — smooth curling locks; kusumāñcita — decked with flowers; capala cāru ure maṇḍita māla — on the restless lovely chest an adorning garland; abhinaba bāhu-bhaṅgī bhara nirupama — in the peerless, ever-new play of the arms; dharata caraṇa-tale sulalita tāla — the feet keep a graceful rhythm

17.3His smooth curling locks are decked with flowers; on His restless, lovely chest — a garland; in the peerless, ever-new play of His arms His feet keep a graceful rhythm.

পহুঁ চলু পাশ লসত প্রিয় পরিকর গায়ত মধুর রাগ রস মাতি ।
উলসিত সকল ভুবন ভণ নরহরি বায়ত খোল খমক বহু ভাঁতি ॥

pahum̐ calu pāśa lasata priya parikara gāyata madhura rāga rasa māti |
ulasita sakala bhubana bhaṇa narahari bāyata khola khamaka bahu bhām̐ti ||

pahum̐ calu — the Lord moves; pāśa lasata priya parikara — beside Him shine the dear associates; gāyata madhura rāga — sing sweet ragas; rasa māti — intoxicated with rasa; ulasita sakala bhubana — the whole world rejoices; bhaṇa narahari — says Narahari; bāyata khola khamaka bahu bhām̐ti — khol and khamak sound in many ways

17.4The Lord moves, beside Him shine the dear associates, singing sweet ragas, intoxicated with rasa; the whole world rejoices, says Narahari; khol and khamak sound in every manner.

18. Narahari — "nācata gauracandra naṭabhūpa…" (GPT1 p. 263, no. 50; BR)

The dance of Gaura, king of dancers: a form crushing the pride of a hundred thousand Kamas; He roars in bhava, spreads His arms, smiles, His face is the autumn moon; the devotees sing, outdoing the kinnaras, the ocean of prema has flooded the earth — only Narahari it does not touch. Raga belavali. Attribution: probably Chakravarti — the pada is in the BR (12th wave); Vrajabuli.56

নাচত গৌরচন্দ্র নটভূপ ।
মনমথ-লাখ-গরব-ভর-ভঞ্জন অখিল-ভুবনজন-রঞ্জন রূপ ॥ ধ্রু ॥

nācata gauracandra naṭabhūpa |
manamatha-lākha-garaba-bhara-bhañjana akhila-bhubanajana-rañjana rūpa || dhru ||

nācata gauracandra naṭa-bhūpa — Gaurachandra dances, king of dancers; manamatha-lākha-garaba-bhara-bhañjana — crushing the pride of a hundred thousand Kamas; akhila-bhubana-jana-rañjana rūpa — a form delighting the people of all the worlds

18.1(Refrain) Gaurachandra dances, the king of dancers: a form crushing the pride of a hundred thousand Kamas — the delight of the people of all the worlds.

অবিরত অতুল ভাবভরে গর গর গরজত অতি অদভুত রুচিকারী ।
মঙ্গলময় পদ ধরত ধরণী পর করত ভঙ্গী ভুজযুগল পসারি ॥

abirata atula bhābabhare gara gara garajata ati adabhuta rucikārī |
maṅgalamaya pada dharata dharaṇī para karata bhaṅgī bhujayugala pasāri ||

abirata atula bhāba-bhare gara gara — ceaselessly seized by peerless bhava; garajata ati adabhuta rucikārī — roars wondrously, beautifully; maṅgalamaya pada dharata dharaṇī para — sets the auspicious feet on the earth; karata bhaṅgī bhuja-yugala pasāri — moves with both arms outspread

18.2Ceaselessly seized by peerless bhava, He roars — wondrously, beautifully;
He sets His auspicious feet on the earth, moves with both arms outspread.

হাসত মধুর অধর মৃদু লাবণি শরদ-চাঁদ জিনি বদন-বিলাস ।
টলমল অরুণ কমলদল-লোচন কৌনে করয় কত রস পরকাশ ॥

hāsata madhura adhara mṛdu lābaṇi śarada-cām̐da jini badana-bilāsa |
ṭalamala aruṇa kamaladala-locana kaune karaya kata rasa parakāśa ||

hāsata madhura — smiles sweetly; adhara mṛdu lābaṇi — the lips soft and lovely; śarada-cām̐da jini badana-bilāsa — the play of the face surpasses the autumn moon; ṭalamala aruṇa kamala-dala-locana — the eyes, red lotus petals, sway; kaune karaya kata rasa parakāśa — who can tell how much rasa He reveals

18.3Sweetly He smiles, His lips soft and lovely, the play of His face surpasses the autumn moon; His eyes, petals of a red lotus, sway: who can tell how much rasa He reveals?

গায়ত মধুর ভকতগণ নব নব কিন্নর-নিকর দরপ করু চূর ।
উথলল প্রেমসিন্ধু মহী ভাসল নরহরি কুমতি পরশ রহু দূর ॥

gāyata madhura bhakatagaṇa naba naba kinnara-nikara darapa karu cūra |
uthalala premasindhu mahī bhāsala narahari kumati paraśa rahu dūra ||

gāyata madhura bhakata-gaṇa naba naba — the devotees sing sweetly ever-new (songs); kinnara-nikara darapa karu cūra — crush the pride of the host of kinnaras; uthalala prema-sindhu — the ocean of prema surged; mahī bhāsala — flooded the earth; narahari kumati — foolish Narahari; paraśa rahu dūra — remained far from its touch

18.4Sweetly the devotees sing ever-new songs, crushing the pride of the host of kinnaras; the ocean of prema has surged and flooded the earth — only foolish Narahari it has not touched.57

19. Narahari — "nācata dvija-kula-candra gaurahari…" (GPT1 p. 264, no. 52; BR)

The dance of Gaurahari, moon of the brahmana line: auspicious feet, absorption in the bhava of the former lila, body thrilling, curls like a cloud on a golden mountain, a garland of malati, His face a snare of Kama; the associates sing, the world sinks in an ocean of happiness. Raga nata. Attribution: probably Chakravarti — the pada is in the BR (12th wave); Vrajabuli.58

নাচত দ্বিজকুলচন্দ্র গৌরহরি ।
মঙ্গলময় ভয়-হরণ চরণযুগ ধরত ধরণী পর পরম ভঙ্গী করি ॥ ধ্রু ॥

nācata dvijakulacandra gaurahari |
maṅgalamaya bhaya-haraṇa caraṇayuga dharata dharaṇī para parama bhaṅgī kari || dhru ||

nācata dvija-kula-candra gaurahari — Gaurahari dances, moon of the twice-born line; maṅgalamaya bhaya-haraṇa caraṇa-yuga — the auspicious fear-removing feet; dharata dharaṇī para — He sets on the earth; parama bhaṅgī kari — in wondrous poses

19.1(Refrain) Gaurahari dances, the moon of the twice-born line;
